But the call-up skew and a whisper above consensus already carry that optimism, and the bar is disputed between two sources, so every finding is capped small. impact_sum +1.1 and impact_scaled +0.65 agree in sign and size.
bar: DISPUTED. Earnings Whispers via Finviz (2026-10-26) gives consensus EPS $1.99 and revenue $4.23B, with the whisper at $2.14: https://finviz.com/news/407862/fox-faces-a-higher-bar-as-world-cup-tail-midterm-ads-and-tubi-collide and https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/FOXA/21349 . Chartmill, quoted through a search snippet (its page returns 403), gives EPS $2.13 and revenue $4.39B, with revenue revised down 2.55% over 3 months: https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/FOX/estimates . Fox gives no quarterly guidance. The two sources disagree, so every finding is capped small. print_vs_bar_pct is sized against $4.23B; against $4.39B it would be about -1.5. Prior-year FQ1 FY26, implied by the EW growth rates, was about $3.74B revenue and about $1.51 EPS.
positioning_check: Equibles (FINRA data), settlement 2026-10-15: 48.84M FOXA shares short, 11.6% of shares outstanding, 13.83 days to cover, up 0.67M from the prior settlement; its model expects about 58M at the 10-30 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/foxa/shortinterest). Chartmill/curvedtrading, settlement 2026-09-30: 48.18M short, about 24.5% of float, 9.66 days to cover (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/FOXA/ownership/short-interest). Short interest rose from about 15.6M (Oct 2025) to about 40-49M after the Roku deal (June 15, 2026). Roku holders receive 0.9693 FOXA per share, so most of this is very likely merger-arb hedging rather than a directional crowded short; that is an inference, not sourced. Arb shorts are hedged, so they are a weak squeeze mechanism. Options (sealed baseline): event-implied move 6.18%, 25d skew -9.92 vol points (calls bid, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 0.21. Run-up: 20d +1.17%, 5d -5.39%, 17% below the 52-week high.

findings.finding: On the Aug 6, 2026 FQ4 call (a primary document), management said fiscal Q1 (Jul-Sep 2026) was 'off to an excellent start': World Cup benefit carried into Q1, weighted to the Television segment, which aired most knockout matches including the record July 19 final; upfront closed with double-digit volume growth and was up in 8 of 10 categories; ad strength 'continue[d] into the first quarter'; Tubi's 35% growth momentum 'continued in the first quarter'. Consensus already builds in +13% YoY revenue to $4.23B, about flat on the record $4.21B FQ4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fox's prints reacted +5.3 (Aug 2026), +7.59 (May 2026), -3.61, +7.73, -3.67, +4.34, +5.18 per the baseline: 5 of 7 up, median |move| 5.18%. The Aug 2026 +5.3% came on a 78% ad-revenue jump. Beats on advertising have mostly been bought.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the call is public and consensus implies +13% revenue and +32% EPS. What is not pinned down is the size of the knockout-stage World Cup revenue booked in Q1; management declined to quantify it. Two estimate sources sit $160M apart on revenue ($4.23B vs $4.39B), so the street has not converged. If this were fully priced, the bar would be single-sourced and the whisper would not sit 7% above the low consensus.
findings.independence: Final viewership record of 38.9M on Fox (Nielsen), confirming the knockout audience was in the quarter: https://www.newscaststudio.com/2026/07/22/fox-2026-world-cup-final-ratings/ . This was known before the Aug 6 call, so it is not independent of management's statement.

findings.finding: Gray Media, a direct local-TV peer, raised its Q3 2026 political ad guide on 2026-09-28, after Fox last spoke: $188-195M, up from $165-185M on Aug 7 (+9% at midpoint), against $8M in Q3 2025. Its core advertising was guided flat to -1% (political crowding out core). Sinclair raised its FY2026 political guide 13%, to at least $375M, with its Q2 report. Fox's management expects a record midterm cycle above the $260M of 2022, concentrated in local stations and Tubi.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Political is a Television-segment line. In FQ4 FY26 'higher political advertising revenue at our Television stations' was one driver of +108% TV advertising, and the stock rose +5.3% (baseline, Aug 2026 print). No separate history isolates political surprises.
findings.why_not_priced: Gray's raise came on a lender-meeting update, not a print, and Fox does not break out political in its guide, so whether the September political pace beat sell-side assumptions for Fox's stations is not visible. If it were priced, the Chartmill revenue consensus would not have drifted down 2.55% over 3 months. Partly priced: AdImpact's record $11.6B cycle forecast (June 11) is widely known.
findings.independence: Sinclair's political guide raise to at least $375M: https://sbgi.net/sinclair-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results/ (Aug 2026, roughly the same time as Fox's call, so only partly after it). AdImpact's $11.6B cycle forecast: https://adimpact.com/blogs/adimpact-reveals-2026-election-cycle-to-reach-record-11.6-billion-in-ad-spending . These are proxies: Fox's 29-station footprint is big-market and differs from Gray's swing-state mix. Net of crowd-out of core advertising, sized small.

findings.finding: Digital investment (Tubi plus FOX One losses) came in under $200M in FY26, against just under $300M in FY25 and a $350M original guide. Management said 'continued bottom-line improvement in this portfolio going into fiscal 2027', and that FOX One churn was 'well below our expectations' and continuing that way into Q1. This supports EBITDA and EPS against the $1.99-$2.13 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Digital loss narrowing was part of the Aug 2026 beat (+5.3%) and the May 2026 beat (+7.59%) per the baseline; it was not reported in isolation.
findings.why_not_priced: No quarterly guide for digital losses is given, so the Q1 cadence of improvement is modelled loosely. The whisper ($2.14) sits above the EW consensus ($1.99), which suggests buy-side EPS expectations already lean toward this upside: partly priced.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1, a different line (costs vs revenue), so independence is low. EW's preview notes the same under-$200M figure: https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/FOXA/21349

findings.finding: The CFO said on Aug 6 that the buyback 'continues unabated through the pendency of the transaction and beyond' ($2B repurchased in FY26; $8.6B, about 36% of shares, since Nov 2019), with the deal closing at about 2.8x net leverage. The Q1 release will show how much was bought in the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated history. The buyback was reaffirmed on the Aug 2026 call, and the stock rose +5.3% on the whole print.
findings.why_not_priced: The pace under Roku-deal financing ($8.3B new debt, 40% equity-funded) is uncertain. A sustained $500M-a-quarter pace would be visible in the release and would reassure on the share-count drift; a slowdown would read as deal-financing strain. The market cannot see which until the release.
findings.independence: Same document as findings 1 and 3. None from a different source.

findings.finding: Roku deal overhang inside the print window. The DOJ issued a Second Request on 2026-09-08 (Fox 8-K item 8.01, 2026-09-09). Semafor (2026-09-24) reported Newsmax's Chris Ruddy and White House allies pressing DOJ antitrust to block the $22B deal. Both companies' shareholders approved it on 2026-10-14 (8-K item 5.07). A shareholder disclosure suit was answered with a supplemental proxy (8-K 2026-10-06). Fox limited deal Q&A on the last call. The Q1 call may update HSR compliance or timing; delay or remedy language would weigh on the stock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 24.9% in the week the deal was announced (June 2026) and set a 52-week low of $48.34, so deal news has moved this stock hard. No print-day deal update has occurred yet.
findings.why_not_priced: The Second Request and the lobbying are public, so they are largely priced. Fox's own read on timing has not been heard since the Second Request, and the release or call is the first chance. If the market had priced a long delay, FOXA would trade at its June lows rather than 30% above its 52-week low.
findings.independence: Fox 8-K on the Second Request: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1754301/000119312526385979/d176496d8k.htm . Shareholder approval: https://thedesk.net/2026/10/shareholders-of-fox-roku-approve-22-billion-takeover-deal/ . TechCrunch on the DOJ's added questions: https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/09/doj-wants-more-answers-on-foxs-22b-roku-deal/

outside_window.finding: Roku reports Q3 2026 after the close on 2026-11-02, with no call or guidance because of the pending deal. That is after the close of the first full session following Fox's bmo print, so FOXA (0.9693 exchange ratio, arb-linked) cannot react inside the window.

DOJ HSR waiting period: it expires 30 days after substantial compliance with the Sept 8 Second Request, and the deal is expected to close in H1 CY2027. A clearance or challenge decision falls well after the window.
